title: C# .NET and Oracle Backend Examples
description: Follow small examples from the Reading List API. The C# and Oracle code needs the local sample tools. Each fragment names its setup; HTTP and browser examples use the running API on localhost:5080.

examples.title: Follow one request and one reply
examples.description: After the local API starts, send this GET request. The reply says that the API process is running. This small check does not connect to Oracle or prove that book requests will work.
examples.output:
HTTP status: 200 OK
JSON body: {"status":"API is running","database":"Not checked"}

examples.title: Check the SDK and build the sample
examples.description: Open a terminal in the downloaded sample's ReadingListApi folder. Check that a .NET 10 SDK is listed. Restore gets the project's packages; build checks the C# code.
examples.output:
The SDK list should include a 10.0.x version.
The final command should report: Build succeeded.
This checks the code; it does not prove Oracle is connected.

examples.title: Check which Oracle account you opened
examples.description: Run this in SQLcl or SQL Developer after connecting with your separate practice account. It shows the database account and service used by this SQL session.
examples.output:
For the course's local setup, the account is READING_APP.
The service should be the one in your connection setting, such as FREEPDB1.
Use the actual service supplied by your Oracle setup.

examples.title: Create the table once
examples.description: Run once as the practice table's owner. If the sample's SQL setup already made this table, skip this command. id is a label, title is text, and is_read accepts only 0 or 1.
examples.output:
Oracle creates one empty table.
The next API insert can ask Oracle to make an id.

examples.title: Describe and check the request body
examples.description: This small request model shows the same title rules as the sample. In an API controller with [ApiController], invalid model values produce a 400 reply before the action uses them.
examples.output:
A title such as "Moon Trip" can pass.
A missing title, whitespace-only title, or title over 120 characters fails.
The request body does not choose the book id.

examples.title: Open a short Oracle connection
examples.description: This fragment belongs in an async C# helper with Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Client imported. connectionString must come from the API's private configuration. SELECT 1 checks this connection without changing data.
examples.output:
1

An error here means the database connection or query needs attention.
A successful /health response alone does not run this check.

examples.title: Connect controller routes in Program.cs
examples.description: These are the two controller lines used in Program.cs. Keep the sample's other setup lines. AddControllers goes before builder.Build(); MapControllers goes after it and before app.Run().
examples.output: The API can match controller route attributes such as [Route("api/books")] and [HttpGet].

examples.title: Read one book with a named id
examples.description: Use inside an async helper with an open OracleConnection named connection. Set bookId to an id returned by POST. The title is read as data; a missing id prints a clear message.

examples.title: Ask the API to add a book
examples.description: Send this from an HTTP tool after the local API and Oracle table are ready. Read the returned id and Location header. An id can have gaps, so save the returned value for later requests.
examples.output:
201 Created
The body has id, title and isRead.
The Location header points to the saved book's /api/books/ address.

examples.title: Change and remove only your new practice book
examples.description: Run in PowerShell with the local sample running. This creates a fresh practice book, reads its real id, marks it read, then removes that same book. Existing book ids are not guessed.
examples.code:
$api = 'http://localhost:5080/api/books'
$book = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $api -Method Post `
  -ContentType 'application/json' `
  -Body '{"title":"Practice book","isRead":false}'
$bookUrl = "$api/$($book.id)"

Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $bookUrl -Method Put `
  -ContentType 'application/json' `
  -Body '{"title":"Practice book","isRead":true}'

Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $bookUrl -Method Delete
examples.output:
The successful PUT and DELETE each return 204 No Content.
They do not need a JSON reply body.
A later GET for this deleted id returns 404.

examples.title: Undo one practice insert
examples.description: Run in an async C# helper with a private connection string and the ODP.NET namespace imported. This fresh connection starts its own transaction. Rollback undoes the inserted row, but its identity number may still be skipped.
examples.output:
Practice insert rolled back.
The inserted practice row does not remain in the table.

examples.title: Test a normal reply and a bad title
examples.description: Use an HTTP tool to send these separately. The first request only checks that the API is alive. The second checks the title rule. A real saved-book test must also call the routes that use Oracle.
examples.code:
GET http://localhost:5080/health HTTP/1.1

### Whitespace is not a valid title.
POST http://localhost:5080/api/books HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{"title":"   ","isRead":false}

### An id must be positive in this sample.
GET http://localhost:5080/api/books/0 HTTP/1.1
examples.output:
GET /health: 200; it does not check Oracle.
POST with only spaces in title: 400.
GET with id 0: 400.

examples.title: Read API data from a browser page
examples.description: Run this in the console of the sample page served at http://localhost:5500. Start the API in Development with Development:CorsEnabled=true. The API must allow that exact origin; localhost and 127.0.0.1 are different origins.
examples.output:
The console shows the saved books, or an empty list.
The browser gets JSON from the API. It never needs an Oracle password.

examples.title: Build and run your local finished copy
examples.description: Run from ReadingListApi in PowerShell after setting your development secrets. Release builds the code with release settings. The Development environment still loads your local secrets. Keep this teaching copy on your own computer.
examples.code:
$env:ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = 'Development'
dotnet build --configuration Release
dotnet run --configuration Release --no-build --no-launch-profile --urls http://localhost:5080
examples.output:
The build should succeed and the API should listen on http://localhost:5080.
Then repeat the saved-book and invalid-input checks from Test the API.
Press Ctrl+C to stop the API.
